flash.per_section: Mean score and share of the section's land squares in each class; permanent water left out.

score.name: Flood risk score (multi-criteria)
score.summary: Each 92 m square of land is rated 1 to 5 on seven criteria (distance to a river, drainage density, elevation, land cover, slope, distance to a road, population density); the ratings are weighted as in Leeonis et al. (2024) and averaged over the section by area. 1 is the least exposed, 5 the most.
citations: Leeonis, A. N., Ahmed, M. F., Halder, B., Mokhtar, M. B., Lim, C. K., Juneng, L. and Khirotdin, R. P. K. (2024). Mitigating flood risk at Shah Alam, Malaysia for sustainable development. Discover Sustainability 5: 352, doi:10.1007/s43621-024-00504-y (criteria and AHP weights).
deviations: A whole state is worked out on 92 m squares, each holding the lowest of the nine GLO-30 heights inside it, with its districts as sections: a district holds far more people than the paper's top class, so population rates 5 in every one and tells them apart not at all.
Rainfall (weight 23) and economic loss (3) are left out: no rain record gives rain square by square and no source gives losses by section. The other seven weights are divided by the 74 left.

The paper's distance classes run to kilometres over a wider area; the distance classes here are ours, in metres for a city, kept for the state. Elevation, slope and population keep the paper's classes.
The drainage density classes (breaks at 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 1.5 km per km2) are ours: the paper's, from a kernel density of the main rivers, do not carry over to mapped drains.
Land cover is ESA WorldCover 2021 rated by us: built-up and water 5, bare ground, wetland and mangrove 4, grassland and cropland 3, shrubland 2, tree cover 1.
Drainage density counts mapped drains and ditches; how much of the state's drainage is mapped differs from place to place, and a high density may mean a well drained area as easily as a wet one.

Population is people per section as in the paper, but from WorldPop 2020 summed by section, not council figures; each square takes its section's rating. Under 1,000 rates 1 and the paper's four ranges 2 to 5.
A section's value is the area-weighted mean of its 92 m squares, not the paper's hotspot analysis.

criteria.source: OpenStreetMap rivers and canals, lines and river water areas ((c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL), the ones app/data/dem was built with.
OpenStreetMap rivers, canals, streams, drains and ditches ((c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL): km of line within 1 km, per km2.
Copernicus DEM GLO-30, the lowest of the nine GLO-30 heights in each 92 m square (3 arc seconds).
ESA WorldCover 2021 (10 m, CC BY 4.0), each class rated and mixed by its share of the square.
Copernicus DEM GLO-30, from the same lowest surface.
OpenStreetMap vehicle roads, service ways left out ((c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL).
WorldPop 2020 constrained population, 100 m (CC BY 4.0), summed over each section: people per section.

score.break_rule: A value at or above a break belongs to the class above it.

validation.wording: Compared with past flood records and the river model; this does not validate either index.
validation.history_counts: Events in history.json naming the section (an event naming several sections counts for each).
validation.wet_share: Share of the section's 90 m squares wet at 1 in 50 years in the river model (sections.json).
validation.flash_metric: Share of the section's land squares in the high or extreme class.
validation.rank_rule: 1 = highest of the n sections; ties share the best rank.
